title: Use of Library Skills & ICT
source_note: Standard Nigerian university 'Use of Library' / library and information science GST curriculum combined with foundational ICT literacy: library classification systems, types of libraries and resources, information literacy and research skills, citation/referencing, and basic computer and internet concepts.

questions.question: The Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC) system organizes library materials primarily by:
options: Subject, using numerical classes from 000 to 999
Alphabetical order of the author's surname only
The size of the book
The date the book was published only
questions.correct_answer: Subject, using numerical classes from 000 to 999
questions.explanation: The DDC organizes knowledge into ten main classes numbered 000 to 999, each representing a broad subject area.

questions.question: In the Dewey Decimal Classification, which class number range is designated for 'Science'?
questions.explanation: In the DDC, the 500s class is designated for Natural Sciences and Mathematics.

questions.question: Which classification system is more commonly used by large academic and research libraries, including many university libraries, as an alternative to the Dewey Decimal system?
options: Library of Congress Classification (LCC)
Universal Product Code
International Standard Book Number (ISBN) system
Barcode Classification System
questions.correct_answer: Library of Congress Classification (LCC)
questions.explanation: The Library of Congress Classification (LCC), which uses letters and numbers, is widely adopted by large academic and research libraries.

questions.question: A library that primarily serves the teaching, learning, and research needs of a university's staff and students is best described as a(n):
options: Academic library
Public library
National library
Special library
questions.correct_answer: Academic library
questions.explanation: An academic library exists specifically to support the teaching, learning, and research activities of an educational institution.

questions.question: A library open to and serving the general population of a community, town, or city is known as a:
options: Public library
Special library
Academic library
National library
questions.correct_answer: Public library
questions.explanation: A public library serves the general public within a defined community, providing free or affordable access to information resources.

questions.question: A library established to preserve a nation's published output and serve as a repository of the country's intellectual heritage is called a:
options: National library
Special library
School library
Mobile library
questions.correct_answer: National library
questions.explanation: A national library serves as the central repository responsible for collecting and preserving a country's published materials and cultural heritage.

questions.question: A library that serves a specific organization, profession, or subject area (e.g., a law firm's or hospital's library) is known as a:
options: Special library
Public library
National library
Digital library only
questions.correct_answer: Special library
questions.explanation: Special libraries serve the specific information needs of an organization, profession, or narrow subject area, such as law or medical libraries.

questions.question: The Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC) in a library is primarily used to:
options: Search and locate library materials electronically
Print physical copies of books
Replace the need for a library building
Serve only as a staff attendance register
questions.correct_answer: Search and locate library materials electronically
questions.explanation: OPAC is an electronic catalogue system that allows users to search for and locate library holdings by title, author, subject, or keyword.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a reference material, typically not allowed to be borrowed out of the library?
options: Encyclopedia
Novel for leisure reading
Newspaper from last week
Textbook for a course
questions.correct_answer: Encyclopedia
questions.explanation: Reference materials such as encyclopedias, dictionaries, and atlases are typically kept in the library for consultation only and are not borrowed.

questions.question: A periodical published at regular intervals (e.g., monthly or quarterly), often containing scholarly articles, is generally referred to as a:
options: Journal
Novel
Atlas
Encyclopedia
questions.correct_answer: Journal
questions.explanation: Journals are periodicals published at regular intervals that typically contain scholarly or professional articles.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'information literacy'?
options: The ability to locate, evaluate, and effectively use information
The ability to read only fiction books
Owning a large personal book collection
Knowing how to operate a photocopier
questions.correct_answer: The ability to locate, evaluate, and effectively use information
questions.explanation: Information literacy refers to the skills needed to identify, locate, evaluate, and effectively use information for a given need.

questions.question: When conducting academic research, evaluating a source for 'credibility' mainly involves checking:
options: The author's expertise, publisher reputation, and evidence of accuracy
Only the color of the book cover
The number of pages in the source
Whether the source is the cheapest available option
questions.correct_answer: The author's expertise, publisher reputation, and evidence of accuracy
questions.explanation: Evaluating credibility involves assessing the author's expertise, the reliability of the publisher, and the accuracy of the presented information.

questions.question: Presenting another person's ideas or words as one's own without proper acknowledgment is known as:
options: Plagiarism
Paraphrasing
Referencing
Citation
questions.correct_answer: Plagiarism
questions.explanation: Plagiarism is the act of using someone else's work or ideas without giving proper credit, which is a serious academic offense.

questions.question: Which of the following referencing/citation styles is commonly used in the social sciences?
options: APA (American Psychological Association) style
SI units style
HTML style
Boolean style
questions.correct_answer: APA (American Psychological Association) style
questions.explanation: APA style is a widely used citation format, particularly common in the social sciences.

questions.question: A properly formatted in-text citation and a corresponding reference list entry both serve to:
options: Acknowledge the original source of information used and allow readers to locate it
Increase the word count of an assignment with no other purpose
Replace the need for original writing entirely
Hide the sources used from the reader
questions.correct_answer: Acknowledge the original source of information used and allow readers to locate it
questions.explanation: Citations and reference lists give credit to original sources and enable readers to locate and verify the cited material.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a computer's 'hardware'?
options: The physical, tangible components of a computer system
The set of instructions that tell a computer what to do
A type of internet browser
A file storage format
questions.correct_answer: The physical, tangible components of a computer system
questions.explanation: Hardware refers to the physical components of a computer, such as the monitor, keyboard, and central processing unit.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes computer 'software'?
options: A set of programs and instructions that direct a computer's operations
The physical casing of the computer
A type of computer memory chip
The electrical cable connecting the computer to power
questions.correct_answer: A set of programs and instructions that direct a computer's operations
questions.explanation: Software refers to programs and instructions that tell computer hardware what tasks to perform.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an operating system?
options: Microsoft Windows
Microsoft Word
Google Chrome
Adobe Photoshop
questions.correct_answer: Microsoft Windows
questions.explanation: Microsoft Windows is an operating system, which manages computer hardware and software resources, unlike Word, Chrome, or Photoshop, which are application programs.

questions.question: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) of a computer is often referred to as the:
options: 'Brain' of the computer
External storage device
Input device only
Printer driver
questions.correct_answer: 'Brain' of the computer
questions.explanation: The CPU processes instructions and performs calculations, earning its description as the 'brain' of the computer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an input device?
options: Keyboard
Monitor
Printer
Speaker
questions.correct_answer: Keyboard
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device used to enter data and commands into a computer, unlike a monitor, printer, or speaker, which are output devices.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an output device?
options: Monitor
Mouse
Keyboard
Scanner
questions.correct_answer: Monitor
questions.explanation: A monitor displays processed data as output, distinguishing it from input devices like a mouse, keyboard, or scanner.

questions.question: Random Access Memory (RAM) in a computer is best described as:
options: Temporary, volatile memory used to store data actively being processed
Permanent storage that retains data even when the computer is off
A type of printer
An internet connection protocol
questions.correct_answer: Temporary, volatile memory used to store data actively being processed
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory used for temporary storage of data and instructions currently being used by the computer; it loses its contents when power is off.

questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes internal memory (like RAM) from secondary storage (like a hard disk)?
options: Secondary storage retains data permanently even without power, while RAM is temporary and volatile
There is no functional difference between the two
RAM stores data permanently, while secondary storage is temporary
Secondary storage is faster than RAM in all computers
questions.correct_answer: Secondary storage retains data permanently even without power, while RAM is temporary and volatile
questions.explanation: Secondary storage devices (like hard disks) retain data even when powered off, while RAM only holds data temporarily during active use.

questions.question: In an internet search engine, using the Boolean operator 'AND' between two keywords will typically:
options: Narrow the search to results containing both keywords
Broaden the search to results containing either keyword
Exclude both keywords from the results
Have no effect on the search results
questions.correct_answer: Narrow the search to results containing both keywords
questions.explanation: The Boolean operator 'AND' narrows search results to only those containing all specified keywords.

questions.question: In a search engine, using the Boolean operator 'OR' between two keywords will typically:
options: Broaden the search to results containing either keyword
Narrow the search to results containing only one specific keyword
Exclude results containing either keyword
Cause a search error
questions.correct_answer: Broaden the search to results containing either keyword
questions.explanation: The 'OR' operator broadens a search by retrieving results that contain at least one of the specified keywords.

questions.question: In a search engine, using the Boolean operator 'NOT' before a keyword will typically:
options: Exclude results containing that keyword
Include only results containing that keyword
Have no effect on search results
Automatically translate the keyword
questions.correct_answer: Exclude results containing that keyword
questions.explanation: The 'NOT' operator excludes search results containing the specified keyword.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes an academic database (such as JSTOR or Google Scholar) in the context of research?
options: A resource that provides access to scholarly articles, journals, and academic publications
A social media platform for casual networking
A tool used only for online shopping
A video streaming service
questions.correct_answer: A resource that provides access to scholarly articles, journals, and academic publications
questions.explanation: Academic databases provide access to scholarly and peer-reviewed publications useful for academic research.

questions.question: A 'peer-reviewed' academic article is one that has:
options: Been evaluated by experts in the field before publication to ensure quality and validity
Never been read by anyone before publication
Been written exclusively by students
Been published without any editorial process
questions.correct_answer: Been evaluated by experts in the field before publication to ensure quality and validity
questions.explanation: Peer review is a quality-control process where experts in the relevant field evaluate a manuscript before it is published.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'electronic mail' (email)?
options: A method of exchanging digital messages over the internet
A physical postal delivery service
A type of computer virus
A printed newsletter
questions.correct_answer: A method of exchanging digital messages over the internet
questions.explanation: Email is a digital communication method that allows users to send and receive messages over the internet.

questions.question: Which of the following is a basic precaution for protecting a personal online account from unauthorized access?
options: Using a strong, unique password and avoiding sharing it with others
Using the same simple password for every account
Sharing login credentials publicly online
Disabling all security settings
questions.correct_answer: Using a strong, unique password and avoiding sharing it with others
questions.explanation: Using strong, unique passwords and keeping them confidential is a fundamental step in protecting online accounts from unauthorized access.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'malware'?
options: Malicious software designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems
A type of productivity software for creating documents
A hardware component for storing files
A type of internet browser
questions.correct_answer: Malicious software designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems
questions.explanation: Malware is malicious software created to harm, exploit, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems and data.

questions.question: Which file format is commonly used to preserve the exact formatting of a document across different devices and software (often used for final, shareable versions)?
options: PDF (Portable Document Format)
MP3
JPEG only
EXE
questions.correct_answer: PDF (Portable Document Format)
questions.explanation: PDF preserves the exact layout and formatting of a document regardless of the device or software used to view it, making it ideal for sharing finished documents.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a library's 'call number'?
options: To indicate the specific location of a book on the shelf based on its classification
To serve as the price of the book
To indicate the number of pages in a book
To serve as a library member's identification number
questions.correct_answer: To indicate the specific location of a book on the shelf based on its classification
questions.explanation: A call number is derived from a classification system and tells the user where to find a specific item on the library shelves.

questions.question: An abstract at the beginning of a research article primarily serves to:
options: Provide a concise summary of the article's purpose, methods, and findings
List all references used in the article
Serve as the article's conclusion only
Replace the need for reading the full article for any purpose
questions.correct_answer: Provide a concise summary of the article's purpose, methods, and findings
questions.explanation: An abstract gives readers a brief overview of an article's purpose, methodology, and key findings, helping them decide whether to read further.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the function of a library's 'circulation desk'?
options: Managing the borrowing and returning of library materials
Repairing damaged computer hardware
Printing academic transcripts
Conducting laboratory experiments
questions.correct_answer: Managing the borrowing and returning of library materials
questions.explanation: The circulation desk is the service point in a library responsible for checking materials in and out to patrons.

questions.question: An 'e-book' is best defined as:
options: A digital version of a book that can be read on an electronic device
A printed book with a plastic cover
A type of library membership card
A physical audio cassette
questions.correct_answer: A digital version of a book that can be read on an electronic device
questions.explanation: An e-book is an electronic, digital version of a book that can be accessed and read using computers, tablets, or e-readers.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes an institutional repository maintained by a university?
options: A digital archive that collects and preserves the institution's scholarly output, such as theses and research papers
A physical storage room for old furniture
A financial account used only for tuition payments
A social media page for the institution
questions.correct_answer: A digital archive that collects and preserves the institution's scholarly output, such as theses and research papers
questions.explanation: An institutional repository digitally collects, preserves, and provides access to a university's scholarly and research output.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of a bibliography or reference list at the end of an academic paper?
options: To list all sources cited or consulted in preparing the work
To list the author's personal achievements
To provide a summary of the paper's introduction
To serve as an advertisement for the publisher
questions.correct_answer: To list all sources cited or consulted in preparing the work
questions.explanation: A bibliography/reference list documents all sources used or consulted, allowing verification and further reading.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes an ISBN (International Standard Book Number)?
options: A unique numeric identifier assigned to a specific published book edition
A person's library membership number
A university course code
A type of internet protocol address
questions.correct_answer: A unique numeric identifier assigned to a specific published book edition
questions.explanation: An ISBN is a unique identifier assigned to a specific edition of a published book, used for cataloging and commerce.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'browser' in the context of using the internet?
options: A software application used to access and view websites
A physical device for scanning documents
A type of computer virus
A storage device for saving files
questions.correct_answer: A software application used to access and view websites
questions.explanation: A web browser (such as Chrome or Firefox) is software used to access, navigate, and display content from the internet.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'search engine'?
options: An online tool that helps users find information on the internet based on keywords
A device used to physically print search results
A type of computer hardware component
An offline library card catalogue only
questions.correct_answer: An online tool that helps users find information on the internet based on keywords
questions.explanation: A search engine is an online tool (such as Google) that retrieves relevant web content based on user-entered keywords.

questions.question: Which of the following is good practice when evaluating a website's reliability for academic research?
options: Checking the author's credentials, the domain type (e.g., .edu, .gov), and publication date
Trusting any website that appears first in search results without further checks
Ignoring the author's identity entirely
Assuming all websites are equally reliable
questions.correct_answer: Checking the author's credentials, the domain type (e.g., .edu, .gov), and publication date
questions.explanation: Evaluating website reliability involves examining the author's expertise, the credibility of the domain, and how current the information is.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'paraphrasing' when used properly in academic writing?
options: Restating another person's ideas in one's own words while still citing the original source
Copying text word-for-word without citation
Deleting the original author's ideas entirely
Submitting someone else's paper as one's own
questions.correct_answer: Restating another person's ideas in one's own words while still citing the original source
questions.explanation: Proper paraphrasing involves rephrasing another's ideas in one's own words while still crediting the original source, avoiding plagiarism.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the function of spreadsheet software such as Microsoft Excel?
options: Organizing, calculating, and analyzing data in rows and columns
Editing photographs
Playing video files
Browsing the internet
questions.correct_answer: Organizing, calculating, and analyzing data in rows and columns
questions.explanation: Spreadsheet software like Excel is designed for organizing, calculating, and analyzing data arranged in rows and columns.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes word processing software such as Microsoft Word?
options: Software used to create, edit, and format text documents
Software used exclusively for numerical calculations
Software used to manage computer hardware drivers
Software used only for internet browsing
questions.correct_answer: Software used to create, edit, and format text documents
questions.explanation: Word processing software is designed for creating, editing, and formatting text-based documents.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes why library users are generally advised to use varied keywords and synonyms when searching a catalogue or database?
options: Different sources may use different terminology, so varied keywords increase the chance of finding relevant materials
Using only one keyword always guarantees complete results
Synonyms are irrelevant to search accuracy
Catalogues only accept a single fixed keyword per search
questions.correct_answer: Different sources may use different terminology, so varied keywords increase the chance of finding relevant materials
questions.explanation: Because different authors and sources may use varying terminology for the same concept, using multiple keywords and synonyms improves search comprehensiveness.

questions.question: 'Interlibrary loan' is a service that allows a library to:
options: Borrow materials from another library on behalf of a patron when the item is unavailable locally
Permanently transfer ownership of books to another library
Prevent patrons from ever borrowing books
Sell surplus books to the public
questions.correct_answer: Borrow materials from another library on behalf of a patron when the item is unavailable locally
questions.explanation: Interlibrary loan allows a library to obtain materials from another library to meet a patron's needs when the item is not held locally.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of portable secondary storage commonly used to transfer files between computers?
options: USB flash drive
Random Access Memory (RAM)
Central Processing Unit (CPU)
Motherboard
questions.correct_answer: USB flash drive
questions.explanation: A USB flash drive is a portable secondary storage device commonly used to transfer or store files between computers.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'cloud storage'?
options: Storing data on remote servers accessible over the internet rather than only on a local device
Storing data exclusively on paper records
A method of storing data only inside a computer's RAM
A type of printer ink cartridge
questions.correct_answer: Storing data on remote servers accessible over the internet rather than only on a local device
questions.explanation: Cloud storage allows users to save and access data on remote servers via the internet, rather than relying solely on local device storage.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'copyright' as it applies to published works in a library?
options: A legal right that protects an author's or creator's exclusive rights over their original work
A requirement that all books must be free of charge
A rule that applies only to unpublished manuscripts
A system for organizing books by color
questions.correct_answer: A legal right that protects an author's or creator's exclusive rights over their original work
questions.explanation: Copyright is a legal protection granting creators exclusive rights over the use and distribution of their original works.
